contextual.summary: Durham makes a reduced contextual offer (shown on each course page) to Home-fee applicants who were eligible for free school meals, or who meet two or more of its other criteria.

criteria.detail: Have been eligible for free school meals (regardless of school type); checked using UCAS-matched government data, not the UCAS self-declared answer
Home postcode is TUNDRA LSOA quintile 1 or 2 and/or TUNDRA MSOA quintile 1 or 2
Home postcode is classified as Censation Affluence level E
Current or most recently attended school is a UK state school (not those at an independent school on a scholarship)

contextual.rulesText: You may be made a contextual offer if you’ve been eligible for free school meals, or if you meet two (or more) of: TUNDRA quintile 1–2 postcode, Censation Affluence level E postcode, UK state school, care-experienced, estranged. Only for Home-fee applicants; use your home address on UCAS and apply by the UCAS equal consideration date. Not available through Clearing.

programmes.name: Destination Durham
programmes.summary: Non-residential access programme for Year 12 and 13 students from the North East, with several campus, department and college visits and an assessed project in a subject of your choice.
programmes.whoCanApply: Year 12 students based in the North East of England at a state school or college, from neighbourhoods with low progression to higher education or high deprivation, with a GCSE score of at least 48 from their top 8 GCSEs (including English Language and Maths).
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Essential: in Year 12 and based in the North East of England; at a state school or college; lived in the UK for at least three years; UK national or settled status; studying subjects related to the chosen subject stream; from a neighbourhood with low progression to higher education or high deprivation (TUNDRA MSOA/LSOA quintiles 1–2 prioritised; ACORN groups N–U considered); total GCSE score of at least 48 from top 8 GCSEs including English Language and Maths. May prioritise: care-experienced, estranged, free school meals, first generation to university.
benefits: Guaranteed alternative offer from Durham, typically two A-level grades below the standard offer, on successful completion (subject requirements apply; Economics needs A-level Maths)
Several visits to campus, departments and colleges
Assessed project in a subject of your choice

programmes.name: Global Futures Pre-University Summer School
programmes.summary: Paid 10-day residential summer school where 16–17 year olds live in a Durham college and follow a 24-hour academic pathway (Arts and Humanities, Science or Social Sciences).
programmes.whoCanApply: Students aged 16–17 for the whole programme who are doing well in their studies (minimum B2 English); applications are made by a parent, guardian or carer, with a short personal statement and a teacher recommendation.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Must be aged 16–17 for the full duration; performing well in current studies; minimum B2 level English. Places are limited and the aim is a diverse international cohort.
benefits: 24 hours of university-level teaching in your chosen pathway
Nine nights in en-suite college accommodation with all meals

notes: All course pages are for September 2027 entry; no 2028-entry course pages were published when checked (2026-10-17).

No admissions test is needed for any of these courses. Durham only uses the TMUA/STEP for its Mathematics and Mathematics and Statistics degrees, where a TMUA score of 5.0+ can mean a one-grade-lower offer.
Durham values the EPQ but it does not form part of its offers.

Durham gives a guaranteed alternative offer (typically two A-level grades below the standard offer) to students who successfully complete its Sutton Trust Summer School, as well as its own Destination Durham, STEP and Asian Access programmes.
Durham has a collegiate system; first-year accommodation is in its colleges (prices vary by college and room type).
